questions.question: Which identity is sufficient to reproduce one daily feature partition?
options: The worker hostname and retry count
The logical interval, input snapshot, transform version, schema version, and parameters
The dashboard timestamp only
The output row count without input identity
questions.explanation: Replay equivalence depends on the logical data and every version that can change its meaning. Attempts and worker hosts are execution details, not the data contract.

questions.question: A recommendation feature must be visible within 15 minutes. Source, transform, quality, and publish work consume 7 minutes. What is the most useful next design step?
options: Adopt streaming without measuring anything else
Allocate the remaining 8 minutes to collection and queue delay, then choose the simplest mode that fits
Remove quality validation
Use a daily batch because the source is durable
questions.explanation: A freshness SLO is a budget. Subtract unavoidable stages first, then select batch, micro-batch, or streaming from the remaining wait allowance.

questions.question: Why does a streaming aggregation need event time and a lateness policy?
options: Workers always receive events in event-time order
Processing time and event time can diverge, so a window needs rules for completeness and later corrections
Event time removes the need for checkpoints
Late records are always invalid
questions.explanation: Events can be delayed or reordered. Watermarks estimate progress, while the lateness policy defines whether later records update, quarantine, or miss a result.

questions.question: A task wrote its output and failed before acknowledging success. Which write pattern makes the retry safest?
options: Append the complete output again
Generate random record identifiers on every attempt
Rebuild a stable logical partition in shadow and atomically replace its published manifest
Disable retries
questions.explanation: A stable partition identity plus isolated build and atomic publication makes repeated attempts converge on one reader-visible result.

questions.question: Which recovery plan best fixes a bad transform across 24 historical partitions?
options: Read the current mutable serving copy and blind-append all results
Replay a versioned raw snapshot into shadow partitions, validate them, and publish with a rollback manifest
Delete the raw data before the backfill
Run all historical intervals at unlimited concurrency
questions.explanation: Versioned input preserves history; shadow output and validation contain risk; atomic manifests support bounded publication and rollback.

questions.question: Which metric most directly tells a training consumer whether usable data is current?
options: Average worker CPU
Age of the newest complete, validated event-time interval
Number of orchestration plugins
Total log volume
questions.explanation: Worker health does not prove data readiness. The age of the newest complete validated interval measures the freshness actually available to the consumer.
